components.css: .ds-rail { font-family: Switzer, Lausanne, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #2E2E28; } .ds-rail-labels, .ds-rail-times { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); } .ds-rail-step { display: block; margin-left: -8px; margin-right: 16px; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-rail-step.is-open { background: #F4F3EF; } .ds-rail-step small { display: block; font-size: 13px; line-height: 20px; color: #707063; } .ds-rail-step small strong { color: #2E2E28; font-weight: 600; margin-left: 6px; } .ds-rail-step b { display: block; font-size: 16px; line-height: 24px; font-weight: 550; } .ds-rail-step em { display: block; font-style: normal; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; color: #707063; } .ds-rail-step.is-pending b { color: #707063; font-weight: 400; } .ds-rail-line { position: relative; margin-top: 12px; height: 3px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #DBDACB; } .ds-rail-line > i { position: absolute; top: -5px; width: 2px; height: 13px; background: #2E2E28; } .ds-rail-line > i.is-pending { background: #DBDACB; } .ds-rail-done { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #2E2E28; transition: width 700ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1); } .ds-rail-now { position: absolute; right: -1px; top: -5px; width: 2px; height: 13px; background: #2E2E28; } .ds-rail-times { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 13px; color: #707063; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
CounterCall looks like a page Ramp could have shipped: white pages, a warm-gray sidebar, warm olive-gray secondary text, hairline dividers, near-square controls and fully round pills. A held bank-change request is shown as one more item that needs a person, not as an alarm. The calm is the argument. The money is frozen, the facts are on the page, and the one lime button belongs to a human.

Density is low and type is large, because the real audience watches a 1280x720 recording or a projector with seconds per screen. Each case page tells one story (email flagged, payments held, vendor called on the number already on file, result) along one continuous timeline rail, with one step open beneath it. A single sentence banner says what happened. Held money is the only warm-orange thing on the screen. Headlines are regular weight (450) and tightly tracked. Amounts and ids stay in the sans with tabular figures, the way Ramp sets them.

There is one light look, used by the landing page, the app and the Remotion video. The `[data-theme]` attributes are inert. Switzer (ITF Free Font License) stands in for Ramp's licensed Lausanne. `scripts/fetch-fonts.mjs` fetches it at build into the gitignored `public/fonts`, and it is never committed. The system rejects the AI-dashboard default: dark mode, rounded card soup, glowing pills, and a status repeated four times.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, warm-gray sidebar and bands, ink text at 5:1+ muted secondary.
Near-square controls, banners and inputs (2px), round pills and avatars, cards at 6px.
One Solar lime primary action per page. Lime also marks evidence and the nav count.
Blaze orange is reserved for held money.
Flat surfaces with hairline borders. The release drawer is the only lifted surface.
Regular-weight display type, sentence case, tabular figures for money.

rules.name: The One Lime Rule
rules.body: An app page carries at most one lime button. Lime elsewhere marks evidence or a count and is never a second call to action.

rules.name: The Blaze Means Held Rule
rules.body: Blaze orange in any form (hatch, tint, ink) says "this money is frozen". Never use it for a warning, a hover or decoration.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every status pairs its tint with a glyph and a word: pause bars for held, a check for verified, a cross for blocked, a triangle for needs a person.

rules.name: The Regular Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines are 450 weight and tightly tracked (-0.02em). Size carries the hierarchy, not boldness.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, tab, button and chip is in sentence case at zero tracking. Nothing is uppercase-tracked.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Amounts, case ids and clocks use tabular figures in the sans.

rules.name: The Tone Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces with a tone step or one hairline. The release drawer is the only surface allowed to float.

dos: Do take every colour, radius and duration from `app/globals.css`. `npm run lint:ui` (`scripts/check-ui.sh`) fails on hex, rgb() or hsl() literals, arbitrary radii, shadows and gradients, transition-all, literal durations, and Tailwind default palette classes anywhere outside `app/globals.css`.
Do keep one lime primary action per app page.
Do use Blaze (hatch, tint, Blaze Ink) only where money is held.
Do pair every status tint with a glyph and a word.
Do set money, ids and clocks with tabular figures in Switzer.
Do use the motion tokens: the standard ease cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), 150-300ms for UI and 400-700ms for story beats, at most 8px of travel, and an instant reduced-motion branch.
Do keep `components/**` presentational (no `next/*`, no fetching), because the Remotion project in `video/` imports them.
Do self-host Switzer through `scripts/fetch-fonts.mjs` into gitignored `public/fonts`.
donts: Don't commit the font files, add a font CDN, or add a second typeface.
Don't add a theme, a dark mode or a second look. The `.night` surface is reserved for the landing call widget and the video end cards.
Don't add shadows or gradients to cards, buttons or pills. The drawer is the one exception.
Don't use a radius above 6px except for full rounds.
Don't bold headlines or uppercase-track labels.
Don't put white text on lime, or let lime become a second call to action.
Don't restate a case's status four ways on one screen. The banner sentence and the step's status word carry it.
